To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fiber nonlinearities, such as four-wave mixing ( FWM) and stimulated Raman scattering( SRS) can have a significant effect on the IP performance in optical networks.
fiber nonlinearities have significant effect on IP packet performance in optical networks.
FWM and the SRS are sensitive to power level and frequency spacing of input light, but each in unique way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of optical nonlinearities on IP traffic performance in optical crossconnects.
the impact of optical nonlinear effects on the IP traffic performance in optical crossconnect-based IP-over-DWDM networks.
the effect of fiber nonlinearity on the performance of optical channels and the impact of the effect of fiber fiber nonlinearity to IP traffic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of IP over GMPLS DWDM network is affected by the nonlinear effects in a very complicated way.
, in the design of IP traffic over optical networks, one should not only consider the nonlinear effect of optical channels, but also take into account the effect of IP traffic on optical channels.
the effect of fiber nonlinearity on the performance of optical IP networks should be considered in the system design, especially for the case of low traffic load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effect of fiber nonlinearity on IP performance is not serious when IP traffic load in such systems is light, and the allowable input light power level is not very sensitive to the frequency spacing between optical wavelengths, but the effect of SRS on IP performance is more serious than that of FWM.

, the effect of nonlinear optical phenomena on the performance of traffic in the optical channel can be significantly reduced if IP traffic load is low, the input optical power is low and the frequency spacing between the channels is large.
FWM is a dominant nonlinear effect for a system with a high traffic load, while SRS dominates for a light traffic load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the IP network can be significantly improved by optimizing the optical parameters in the DWDM system.

, when IP traffic load and input power level are light in such systems and when the frequency spacing of adjacent channels is large enough, the worst-case assumption of FWM and SERS may be relaxed, and the performance of IP packet error can be improved significantly.
the effect of fiber nonlinearity on IP packet error rate can be significantly reduced by proper design and optimization of optical network.
